questions.q: Why is mean absolute error (MAE) a convenient headline metric for a price model?
options: It is the only metric scikit-learn supports for regression
It is always smaller than RMSE and R-squared
It ignores the size of errors entirely
It is the average miss in the target's own units, dollars, which anyone can interpret
questions.explain: MAE is the average absolute miss expressed in the same units as the target, which makes it easy to explain to non-technical stakeholders.

questions.q: What does TransformedTargetRegressor with func=np.log1p and inverse_func=np.expm1 do?
options: Trains on the log of the target and converts predictions back to the original scale
Applies a log transform to every feature column
Removes outliers from the training set
Replaces cross-validation
questions.explain: The regressor is fit to the transformed target, and predictions are passed through the inverse function so they come back in dollars.

questions.q: In the lesson, the log target lowered error for gradient boosting but raised it for ridge. What does that teach?
options: Log targets always hurt linear models
Cross-validation results are random and unusable
A transformation should be tested per model rather than assumed to help
Ridge cannot use a transformed target
questions.explain: The effect of a transformation depends on the model and data. Measure it with cross-validation instead of assuming.

questions.q: The residual plot shows a funnel that widens as predicted price rises. What does it mean?
options: The model is perfect
The test set is contaminated
The features were not scaled
Errors are larger for expensive homes, so accuracy is uneven across the price range
questions.explain: A widening residual spread (heteroscedasticity) means dollar errors grow with price. It is worth reporting and may justify percentage-error metrics.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the mean-price baseline (DummyRegressor)?
options: To give a minimum performance every real model must beat, here about $98,000 MAE
To choose the neighborhood encoding
To speed up cross-validation
To replace the test set
questions.explain: The baseline shows what you get without any learning. A model is only useful to the extent it improves on it.
